Red to move. Mate in one.
Five chapters of real campaigns. Each battle ends on a checked mate in one. The position is an exercise, not a reconstruction of the historical game.
Lu, 684 BC. Cao Gui let Qi beat the drums three times, then struck. Mate in one: iron bolt.
632 BC. Jin drew the Chu center forward and closed both wings. Mate in one: double rooks.
506 BC. Wu drove deep into Chu and took Ying. Mate in one: horse behind the cannon.
478 BC. Yue crossed the river in two bodies and broke Wu. Mate in one: pocket horse.
354 BC. Qi marched on Wei’s capital to lift the siege of Zhao. Mate in one: double cannon.
342 BC. Sun Bin reduced his campfires and waited in the pass. Mate in one: fishing horse.
260 BC. Qin cut Zhao’s army off and closed the ring. Mate in one: double rooks.
279 BC. Tian Dan opened the city and drove into the Yan camp at night. Mate in one: pocket horse.
204 BC. Han Xin put his army with its back to the river, then turned. Mate in one: face-to-face generals.
206 BC. The plank road was a feint. The army came out at Chen Cang. Mate in one: double cannon.
204 BC. Han Xin dammed the river, drew the enemy across, then let the water go. Mate in one: horse behind the cannon.
202 BC. Han armies closed on Xiang Yu from every side. Mate in one: double rooks.
AD 200. Cao Cao burned Yuan Shao’s supplies at Wuchao. Mate in one: iron bolt.
AD 208. Fire ran through the chained fleet on the Yangtze. Mate in one: double cannon.
AD 219. Huang Zhong took Dingjun Mountain and Xiahou Yuan fell. Mate in one: fishing horse.
AD 222. Lu Xun held back, then burned the Shu camps. Mate in one: pocket horse.
383. Fu Jian’s host started to fall back and could not be stopped. Mate in one: face-to-face generals.
621. Li Shimin broke Dou Jiande in front of the pass. Mate in one: corner horse.
1140. Yue Fei’s riders broke the Jin cavalry at Yancheng. Mate in one: horse behind the cannon.
1363. Zhu Yuanzhang’s fire ships broke Chen Youliang’s tower ships. Mate in one: heaven-and-earth cannons.
